subject: How to provide valid ID type in check_markers function

messages.author: 97dd7aacdca5ec80
messages.subject: How to provide valid ID type in check_markers function
parts:
Hi,

I am working on with Arabidopsis on Garnett. When I provided arguments in check_markers function, I got an error showing the use of default column ENSEMBL, even though I changed the type to TAIR. ENSEMBL not in the columns of org.At.tair.db. How do I replace the default argument?

Thanks,

RS

Code:

> marker_check <- check_markers(ara_cds, "E:/example_data/marker_file.txt",
+                               db = org.At.tair.db,
+                               cds_gene_id_type = "TAIR",
+                               marker_file_gene_id_type = "TAIR")
Error in .testForValidCols(x, cols) :
  Invalid columns: ENSEMBL. Please use the columns method to see a listing of valid arguments.


> columns(org.At.tair.db)
 [1] "ARACYC"       "ARACYCENZYME" "ENTREZID"     "ENZYME"       "EVIDENCE"     "EVIDENCEALL"  "GENENAME"     "GO"           "GOALL"      
[10] "ONTOLOGY"     "ONTOLOGYALL"  "PATH"         "PMID"         "REFSEQ"       "SYMBOL"       "TAIR"       
>

messages.author: 027760d088a56515
messages.subject: Re: How to provide valid ID type in check_markers function
parts:
Hi RS,

Thanks for bringing this to my attention. Garnett converts everything to ENSEMBL IDs automatically so that the classifiers can be portable... I’ll need to figure out a fix for organisms without ENSEMBL in their databases. I’ve added it as an issue here: 
https://github.com/cole-trapnell-lab/garnett/issues/2 and can hopefully get to it in the next few days.

Best,
Hannah

messages.subject: Re: How to provide valid ID type in check_markers function
parts:
Hi RS,

I pushed a fix that will hopefully solve this problem in version 0.1.1. Go ahead and redownload/install and give it a try. You will now include an extra argument classifier_gene_id_type which will specify which gene id type to use when training the classifier (set it to "TAIR"). If you run into any problems, go ahead and reopen the issue above.

Best,
Hannah
